import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32

RECIPE = {"n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "ppo_epochs": 3, "gamma": 0.97, "lr": 0.001}


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        s = self.stem(obs)
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
LAND = 16
HID = 32


class FootHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, land, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        n = len(self.fps)
        self.land = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(c, land, 1) for _ in range(n)])
        self.landp = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(2 * land, hid, 1) for _ in range(n)])
        self.cellp = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(c, hid, 1) for _ in range(n)])
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * hid, hid, 1) for _ in range(n)])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in range(n)])

    def forward(self, f):
        Y = f.shape[2]
        X = f.shape[3]
        res = []
        for k, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            l = self.land[k](f)
            q = F.pad(l, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            lmax = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            lavg = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            a = self.landp[k](torch.cat([lmax, lavg], dim=1))
            c = self.cellp[k](f)
            cp = F.pad(c, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            hs = []
            for i in range(dy):
                for j in range(dx):
                    hs.append(F.relu(cp[:, :, i:i + Y, j:j + X] + a))
            h = torch.stack(hs, dim=0)
            z = torch.cat([h.amax(0), h.amin(0), h.mean(0)], dim=1)
            z = F.relu(self.mix[k](z))
            res.append(self.outs[k](z))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = FootHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, LAND, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

        s = self.stem(obs)
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))

import math
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
LAND = 16
HID = 32
HEADS = 4

RECIPE = {"n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "ppo_epochs": 3, "gamma": 0.97, "lr": 0.001}


class FootHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, land, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        n = len(self.fps)
        self.land = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(c, land, 1) for _ in range(n)])
        self.landp = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(2 * land, hid, 1) for _ in range(n)])
        self.cellp = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(c, hid, 1) for _ in range(n)])
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * hid, hid, 1) for _ in range(n)])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in range(n)])

    def forward(self, f):
        Y = f.shape[2]
        X = f.shape[3]
        res = []
        for k, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            l = self.land[k](f)
            q = F.pad(l, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            lmax = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            lavg = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            a = self.landp[k](torch.cat([lmax, lavg], dim=1))
            c = self.cellp[k](f)
            cp = F.pad(c, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            hs = []
            for i in range(dy):
                for j in range(dx):
                    hs.append(F.relu(cp[:, :, i:i + Y, j:j + X] + a))
            h = torch.stack(hs, dim=0)
            z = torch.cat([h.amax(0), h.amin(0), h.mean(0)], dim=1)
            z = F.relu(self.mix[k](z))
            res.append(self.outs[k](z))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class CellAttn(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, heads):
        super().__init__()
        self.h = heads
        self.d = c // heads
        self.pos = nn.Linear(2, c)
        self.ln1 = nn.LayerNorm(c)
        self.qkv = nn.Linear(c, 3 * self.h * self.d)
        self.o = nn.Linear(self.h * self.d, c)
        self.ln2 = nn.LayerNorm(c)
        self.ff1 = nn.Linear(c, 2 * c)
        self.ff2 = nn.Linear(2 * c, c)

    def forward(self, f):
        B, C, Y, X = f.shape
        ys = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, Y, device=f.device, dtype=f.dtype)
        xs = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, X, device=f.device, dtype=f.dtype)
        gy = ys.view(Y, 1).expand(Y, X)
        gx = xs.view(1, X).expand(Y, X)
        coords = torch.stack([gy, gx], dim=-1).reshape(Y * X, 2)
        t = f.flatten(2).transpose(1, 2) + self.pos(coords).unsqueeze(0)
        n = Y * X
        u = self.ln1(t)
        qkv = self.qkv(u).view(B, n, 3, self.h, self.d).permute(2, 0, 3, 1, 4)
        q = qkv[0]
        k = qkv[1]
        v = qkv[2]
        att = torch.softmax(torch.matmul(q, k.transpose(-1, -2)) / math.sqrt(self.d), dim=-1)
        y = torch.matmul(att, v).transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, n, self.h * self.d)
        t = t + self.o(y)
        t = t + self.ff2(F.relu(self.ff1(self.ln2(t))))
        return t.transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, C, Y, X)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.attn = CellAttn(WIDTH, HEADS)
        self.head = FootHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, LAND, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        s = self.stem(obs)
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        f = F.relu(self.attn(f))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

        X = f.shape[3]
        res = []
        for k, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            l = self.land[k](f)
            q = F.pad(l, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))

            lavg = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)

            cp = F.pad(c, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
D = 24
PROJ = 32
HID = 32

RECIPE = {"n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 8, "ppo_epochs": 2, "gamma": 0.98, "gae_lambda": 0.95, "ent_coef": 0.005, "lr": 0.001}


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = int(spec.Z)
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in spec.footprints]
        Z = self.Z
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.layer_in = nn.Linear(4, D)
        self.zemb = nn.Embedding(Z, D)
        self.ctx = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, D, 1)
        self.layer_mid = nn.Linear(D, D)
        self.hgt = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, Z + 1, 1)
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, PROJ, 1)
        nin = 6 * D + 3 * PROJ + 1
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(nin, HID, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, C, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        s = self.stem(obs)
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))

        per = obs[:, :4 * Z].reshape(B, 4, Z, Y, X).permute(0, 2, 3, 4, 1)
        e = self.layer_in(per)
        ctx = self.ctx(f).permute(0, 2, 3, 1).unsqueeze(1)
        zid = torch.arange(Z, device=obs.device)
        ze = self.zemb(zid).view(1, Z, 1, 1, D)
        g = F.relu(e + ctx + ze)
        g = F.relu(self.layer_mid(g))
        g = g.permute(0, 1, 4, 2, 3).reshape(B, Z * D, Y, X)

        hp = torch.softmax(self.hgt(f), dim=1)
        logc = torch.log(torch.cumsum(hp, dim=1).clamp(1e-6, 1.0))
        p = self.proj(f)

        res = []
        for k, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                lc = logc
                gmx, gmn, gav = g, g, g
                pmx, pmn, pav = p, p, p
            else:
                pd = (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1)
                lc = F.avg_pool2d(F.pad(logc, pd), (dy, dx), stride=1) * float(dy * dx)
                gq = F.pad(g, pd)
                gmx = F.max_pool2d(gq, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                gmn = -F.max_pool2d(-gq, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                gav = F.avg_pool2d(gq, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                pq = F.pad(p, pd)
                pmx = F.max_pool2d(pq, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                pmn = -F.max_pool2d(-pq, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                pav = F.avg_pool2d(pq, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            cm = torch.exp(lc)
            pl = cm - F.pad(cm[:, :-1], (0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0))
            wl = pl[:, :Z].unsqueeze(2)
            wb = (1.0 - cm[:, :Z]).clamp_min(0.0).unsqueeze(2) / float(Z)
            gp = torch.cat([gmx.view(B, Z, D, Y, X), gmn.view(B, Z, D, Y, X),
                            gav.view(B, Z, D, Y, X)], dim=2)
            land = (wl * gp).sum(1)
            below = (wb * gp).sum(1)
            feat = torch.cat([land, below, pl[:, Z:Z + 1], pmx, pmn, pav], dim=1)
            h = F.relu(self.mix[k](feat))
            res.append(self.outs[k](h))
        place = torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)

        gl = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(gl)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(gl).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)

analyses.1: There are no results yet, and scores stay hidden, so these choices come from reasoning about the task, not from evidence. To place a brick correctly the agent needs the landing layer under each footprint (the highest column under it). It then needs to know, for every cell of the footprint, whether the target has a cell at exactly that layer with nothing missing below it. The starting head pools each projected channel separately, so it cannot easily link the landing layer found by a max over the footprint to the target at that layer in each cell. Candidates: (1) the starting network with a recipe that gives more, smaller updates, fewer epochs (so more samples) and a longer horizon; (2) a footprint head where the landing features are shared back to every cell of the footprint before the per-cell match is pooled; (3) that head plus one attention layer over all cells, for planning across the whole board, using the same recipe as (1).
analyses.2:
All three round-1 trials trained without errors. Scores are hidden, so we cannot tell which is better and have to choose candidates on prior reasoning. Each candidate should still answer a clear question.
- r1c3 changed two things at once: attention and the recipe. The landing head with the recipe alone has not been tested, so we cannot separate their effects.
- The baseline trunk sees only a 5x5 area around each cell. Order mistakes such as sealing a gap or building an overhang too early can depend on the whole 8x8 board.
- r1c1 tested more updates at 3 epochs. Trading sample reuse for more fresh designs (2 epochs, about 230k steps) has not been tested. With fresh random targets, sample count may matter more than reuse.

This round's candidates:
- **A:** landing head plus the round-1 recipe. This isolates what the attention block adds.
- **B:** a deeper, dilated trunk that sees the whole board, with a broadcast of global context.
- **C:** the baseline network with a recipe that collects more samples and uses a longer horizon.
analyses.3: No scores are visible. All 6 trials trained without errors, so these choices rest on reasoning, not results. Two things have been tested so far. One is the recipe: fewer epochs give more fresh samples and more updates. The other is the head: telling the network about the landing layer. Attention and dilation give global context, but on an 8x8 board they are probably less important than judging one placement correctly. A placement is right if the brick lands at the right layer and every footprint cell at that layer is missing from the build, with no target cells sealed underneath. This round has three parts. (1) Combine the landing-aware FootHead with the 2-epoch, larger-sample recipe. That pairing has not been tried yet. (2) A new head that learns a height distribution per column, works out the landing-layer distribution of the footprint by multiplying CDFs, and reads learned per-layer features at that layer and below it. (3) Push the recipe further, to 1 epoch, to measure how much sample count matters.
analyses.4: No scores are visible, so I have to choose using priors and the structure of the design space. Every trial trained without errors. Two ideas look like the most promising directions. First, the FootHead, which pairs landing information with each cell, targets the main skill the task needs: judging whether a placement is correct and sealing nothing it shouldn't. Second, recipes with fewer epochs give more fresh designs, and the budget favours that because training designs never repeat. These two ideas have only been combined at 2 epochs (r3c1). The deep dilated trunk with a global summary (r2c2) is the only test of wider context without attention, and it was never paired with the FootHead or the 2-epoch recipe. Because this is the final round and selection uses real 2-seed scores, I propose three strong combinations that differ from each other. Each one adds a single change on top of the FootHead with fewer epochs, which raises the chance that at least one beats the start.
